name: Design with Intent
description: A design method and toolkit for deliberately influencing user behavior through interface and product design choices, organized into distinct 'lenses' (e.g. architectural, security, persuasive, visual, cognitive) that a designer can apply to intentionally shape how people interact with a system.
design_relevance_note: A named, structured framework (not just a single bias) for deliberately designing toward or against a behavior -- directly usable as a design-review checklist for whether a product's influence on users is intentional, disclosed, and defensible, rather than an incidental side effect discovered after launch.
prevalence_note: Known specifically within behavior-change design and design-ethics practice (particularly UK/European HCI and design-research circles where Lockton's own work is based), but not a mainstream named framework in general product-design or CRO discourse.

findings.description: Introduces the Design with Intent Method — a structured ideation tool that translates behavior-change intentions into concrete product/system design concepts — demonstrated on a real design problem (reducing the likelihood of customers leaving cards in ATMs).
findings.source_title: The Design with Intent Method: A design tool for influencing user behaviour
